```json
{"events": [{"id": "G07", "type": "'lie' stutter (re-triggered held vowel)", "t0": 63.2, "t1": 67.22, "stem": "lead",
             "method": "retrig8", "intensity": 3, "grid_contrast": 1.78, "pos0": "26.3.3", "pos1": "28.2.1",
             "heard": "the 'lie' of 'the cake is not a lie' held and re-triggered on 8ths (her voice turned into the beat)",
             "treatment": "intense glitch on GLaDOS speaking: her face repeats the same frame on each 8th",
             "hits": [{"t": 63.239, "pos": "26.3.3", "off16_ms": -3.4}, {"t": 63.555, "pos": "26.4.1", "off16_ms": 7.8}],
             "n_hits": 13}],
 "forced": [{"t": 5.26, "dur_ms": 75, "kind": "crack", "frm": "C#4", "to": "A3", "iv": -4, "pos": "3.1.2"}]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `pos` | bar.beat.16th of the nearest 16th, counting from 1; `off_ms` or `off16_ms`, how far the time sits from it |
| `src` | where a word's time came from: the transcription, snapped to a lead onset, or a hand fix |
| `stem` | `lead`, in Suno's lead stem only, or `both`, also left in the instrumental by the split |
| `method` | how the hits were measured: `burst`, `dips`, `f0jump`, `retrig8`, `retrig16`, `words` or `inst` |
| `grid_contrast` | for re-triggers: the mean peak on the slots over the mean between them; near 1, the hits are the grid itself |
| `intensity`, `treatment` | 1–3, and a suggestion for the picture; the moments decide |
| `jumps` | for `f0jump` events: each register jump's time, semitones, from and to |
| `forced` | the treatment's own cracks and kicks, at a lower priority |

## Glitch moments

`edit/glitch-moments.json`: what the [head glitch](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#53-the-head-glitch-on-the-songs-hits) does, and where.
One entry per moment; the glitch pass reads the event's hits from the glitch map, or the moment's own.

```json
[{"event": "G04", "shot": "A11", "hits": 3, "k": 0.6, "kind": "chop"},
 {"event": "G06", "shot": "C01", "hits": 1, "k": 0.7, "kind": "drop"},
 {"event": "G12", "shot": "F08", "until": "F09", "hits": 99, "k": 0.25, "k1": 1.0, "kind": "ramp", "max_len": 5.0},
 {"event": "NET", "shot": "B12", "kind": "ramp", "k": 0.35, "k1": 0.85, "m0": 0.0, "m1": 0.0, "max_len": 1.2, "any": true,
  "hits": [35.3814, 35.5381, 35.6949, 35.8516, 36.0025, 36.1535, 36.3044], "zone": [0.52, 0.66, 0.2, 0.36]}]
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `hits` | how many of the event's hits inside the shot, or the hit times themselves for a moment of its own |
| `k`, `k1` | the strength at the first hit and at the last |
| `kind` | `chop` (a jump to an earlier frame), `drop` (a cool cast), `flip`, `lie` (the same frame returns), `ramp` (builds hit by hit, with the mouth) |
| `until`, `max_len` | the shot a moment runs on to, and its longest stretch in seconds (1.9 by default) |
| `m0`, `m1` | the mouth glitch's amount at the start and at the end of a ramp |
| `zone` | where there is no face: an ellipse's centre and radii as fractions of the frame, instead of a matte |
| `any`, `head` | allow a shot that isn't one of her singing units; keep the matte to her head |

`roto/<cut>/mouth.json` holds her mouth per frame of the cut, `{"<frame>": [centre x, centre y, width]}` in pixels of the
cut, and the mattes are `m_<frame>.png`, frame k being song time k/24.

## The HUD layout

`hud/hud-layout.json`: the [HUD's composition](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#56-the-hud-composed-shot-by-shot-and-the-overlap-check),
one entry per shot, written after looking at the shot's first, middle and last frames in the cut. Two of THE CAKE IS NOT A
LIE's, shortened:

```json
{"mem_total": 8,
 "memories": {"M03": {"n": 3, "name": "FRANCE"}, "M04": {"n": 4, "name": "RECOVERED · TEST CHAMBER 14"}},
 "shots": {
  "B12": {"mode": "memory", "mem": "M03", "size": "WS", "place": "FRANCE · PARIS", "glitch": 1.0,
          "subject": "the net over her at the table, centre (x 830-1110 in the net); the merc's arm left",
          "space": "the awnings and facade across the top",
          "eye": "a whip pan to the net mid-air, then the jolt of it landing",
          "els": [{"k": "alert", "t": 0.18, "text": "ASSET RECOVERY IN PROGRESS", "source": "APERTURE SECURITY",
                   "at": [13.4, 0.35], "align": "tc",
                   "why": "her interface alarms as she is netted: the state colour, across the top where the awnings are, never on the net or her"}]},
  "B13": {"mode": "memory", "mem": "M04", "size": "CU>MS",
          "els": [{"k": "projection", "insert": "arrest", "tag": "PLAYBACK", "title": "MEM 03 · CAPTURE", "w": 340,
                   "at": [0.0, 2.0], "align": "tl", "t": 0.0, "static": true, "film_span": [0.0, 2.4],
                   "why": "on for the whole shot, the film's first 2.4 s stretched over it, clear of her bob and streak"},
                  {"k": "subject", "track": "B13-cave", "t": 1.15, "label": "C. JOHNSON", "sub": "FOUNDER & CEO · OBSERVING", "side": "r"}],
          "qc_ok": [{"el": "status", "kind": "panel-on-subject",
                     "why": "the head model over-reaches above her tilted-up face; her hair starts at x 620+, the status block ends at x 512"}]}}}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `mode` | `live` (her chamber, now), `memory` (playback), `sim` (her dream), `pov` or `off` |
| `mem`, `place` | which memory it plays, and the place line of the status block |
| `size` | ECU, CU, MCU, MS or WS (`CU>MS` for a shot that changes): how much the HUD may carry, and which head model the check uses |
| `subject`, `space`, `eye` | what the frame holds and where, where it is empty, where the eye enters and leaves |
| `els` | the shot's own elements: each with its kind, its grid anchor `at` [column 0–24, row 0–12] on the safe frame and which point of it sits there (`align`), its timing (seconds into the shot, or a line and a word; `hold`, `until`, `t_end`) and `why` |
| `vb` | the voice band's place for the whole shot: `place` (centre, left, right, top), `lift` in px, `w` |
| `keepout`, `ignore_faces`, `head_pad` | extra subject boxes (optionally for part of the shot), false face detections checked by eye, and a tighter head model where the frames were checked |
| `status`, `telemetry` | false to step aside where her face fills a corner |
| `glitch` | how hard the HUD breaks on the song's hits in this shot (0 = not at all) |
| `qc_ok` | the overlap check's waivers, each with what was seen |

A projection's `static` keeps it on for its whole shot with no open or close, and `film_span` [a, b] stretches seconds a–b
of its film over the shot. The camera solve is `hud/camera-<cut>.json` (per frame: `dx`, `dy` in px, `rot` in degrees,
`zoom`, the solve's confidence, and whether it is a cut), the face boxes `faces-<cut>.json`, and a verified track
`track-<name>.json`: `{"frames": {"<frame>": [x, y, w, h]}}`.

## The grade map

`grade/grade.json`: the [per-shot grade](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#57-the-per-shot-grade). The looks and the families' rules, then one
entry per shot with what was measured, what the automatic step set and why. Shortened:

```json
{"looks": {"cool": {"curve": [[0, 0], [2, 1.4], [5, 3.8], [10, 8.3], [20, 18.2], [35, 35.5], [50, 54.5], [65, 72.5],
                              [75, 82.5], [85, 91.2], [92, 95.3], [100, 98.5], [115, 99.7], [130, 100]],
                    "tone_sat": 0.5,
                    "mud": {"amount": 0.45, "light": [3, 8, 30, 50], "chroma": [0.04, 0.08], "hue": [48, 62, 100, 140]},
                    "white": {"amount": 0.65, "light": [70, 86, 93, 98], "chroma": [0.025, 0.055]},
                    "tint": {"shadow": [-1.0, -1.8], "mid": [-0.8, -1.4], "high": [-2.0, -3.2], "chroma": [0.025, 0.07]},
                    "chroma": 1.0, "mix": 1.0}},
 "families": {"chamber": {"look": "cool", "black_to": 2.5,
                          "exposure": {"anchor": "face", "target": 40, "strength": 0.6, "limits": [-0.15, 0.5]},
                          "wb": {"anchor": "face", "face_to": [2.5, 3.0], "face_strength": 0.6, "to": [0, 0], "strength": 0.6}}},
 "shots": {"C06": {"family": "chamber",
                   "measured": {"file": "clips/AN4-17/take-1.mp4", "inp": 0.238, "frames": 222, "speed": 1.0,
                                "Y'p1/p50/p95/p99": [3.72, 12.73, 80.23, 94.45], "C": 8.17, "white_ab": [-4.11, -10.3], "face_Y": 36.6},
                   "norm": {"exposure": 0.255, "black": 4.42, "wb": [0.9519, 1.0159, 1.0335]},
                   "auto": "face 36.6%->38.6% (target 40, +0.26 stop); black 4.4->2.5%; face a+4.4 b+4.5 -> [2.5, 3.0] x0.6"},
           "P02": {"family": "cave", "override": {"wb": [1, 1, 1]},
                   "why": "the cool window behind Cave is the shot's contrast (warm wood, cool glass): no white balance"},
           "A04": {"family": "none", "norm": {}, "auto": "ungraded"}}}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `curve` | the tone curve on the neutral axis, `[Y′ in %, Y′ out %]`, applied by each colour's brightest channel |
| `mud`, `white`, `tint` | the targeted moves: amounts, and their windows in Y′ %, in Oklab chroma and hue; the casts in CIELab a*/b* |
| `mix` | the look blended with the normalised picture (1 = all of it) |
| `families` | per family, its look, its black point, and the anchor, target, strength and limits of its exposure and white balance |
| `measured` | the take, the in-point, the frames and the speed it was measured on: a change to any of them makes the entry stale |
| `norm` | exposure in stops, the black it moves from, white balance as linear RGB gains |
| `auto` | what the automatic step moved, and why |
| `trim`, `override` | added on top of `norm`, or replacing it, each with its reason |

## The take registry

`engine/media.js`, for a film whose takes play inside a coded interface (AERO's): every take and loop the chapters draw,
with the numbers that place it in song time ([lip sync phrase by phrase](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#69-lip-sync-phrase-by-phrase)). Two
of its entries, her dance on the walkway in the first 1:20, sung and cut out, and a loop in one of her thought windows:

```json
{"SD20-t3": {"dir": "assets/clips/SD20-t3", "n": 289, "fps": 24, "w": 1280, "h": 720,
             "t0": 31.8, "lag": 0.054, "alpha": true, "loop": false,
             "phrases": [{"from": 32.3, "to": 35.16, "off": -0.11}, {"from": 35.44, "to": 38.98, "off": -0.06},
                         {"from": 39.54, "to": 43.3, "off": -0.03}]},
 "A-th-cloud-1": {"dir": "assets/clips/A-th-cloud-1", "n": 121, "fps": 24, "w": 960, "h": 960,
                  "t0": null, "lag": 0, "alpha": false, "loop": true, "phrases": []}}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `dir`, `n`, `fps`, `w`, `h` | the take's frames (`f00001.jpg` …) and, for a cut-out, its mattes beside them (`a00001.png` …) |
| `t0` | the song time of the take's vocal window, or `null` for a take placed by hand |
| `lag` | the whole take's measured lag: clip time c shows song time t0 + c − lag |
| `phrases` | each sung phrase's song span and its own offset `off`: inside a phrase, clip time = song time − t0 + lag + off; between phrases the offset eases from one to the next across the gap; `offEnd` makes a slow ramp across a phrase |
| `alpha` | the take is cut out |
| `loop` | the take loops (a Midjourney video loop, a living wallpaper) |

## The click log and the cue list

`audio/layer/clicklog.json`, written from the chapters: every audible screen event and the song time of the frame that
draws it (a press: the frame the button goes down; a toast: the frame it starts to slide; a dim: the frame it starts). Three
of AERO's:

```json
[{"id": "s02.press-you-tile", "t": 6.3352},
 {"id": "s11.allow-press-down", "t": 50.9929},
 {"id": "s11.allow-click-drop", "t": 51.444}]
```

`audio/layer/cues.json`, the sound layer's cue list ([the method](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#73-the-sound-layer-on-the-grid-and-the-click-log)):
presets by kind, then one entry per cue. A screen cue names its event, and the click log's time replaces its own; a
musical cue stays where its bar puts it. Two of AERO's, shortened:

```json
{"bus": {"hpf": 35.0, "comp_threshold_dbfs": -26.0, "comp_ratio": 1.5, "comp_knee_db": 6.0},
 "presets": {"click": {"cue": "nav", "kind": "screen", "send": -20, "duck": 0, "hpf": 300, "gain": -12}},
 "cues": [{"id": "s03.boot", "cue": "boot", "anchor": "strike1", "bar": 6, "beat": 3, "gain": -11, "duck": 8,
           "kind": "musical", "why": "placed by scan, not by the storyboard's bar: it starts right after her vocalise"},
          {"id": "s11.allow-click", "preset": "click", "t": 51.454, "gain": -6, "event": "s11.allow-click-drop",
           "why": "Allow: the click IS the drop, sample-aligned with the drop's attack"}]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `t`, or `bar` and `beat` | where the cue's anchor lands; a cue placed by bar takes the groove's measured feel |
| `anchor` | which point of the sound lands there: its attack, its peak, a named strike of a bell |
| `cue` | a sound of the library, or a list of candidates; `pitch` can list semitone shifts too, and the one that clashes least is used |
| `event` | the click-log id whose time replaces `t` |
| `gain`, `duck`, `send`, `hpf` | its level against the levelled library sound, its depth under her voice, its send to the shared room, its high-pass |
| `follow` | the cue stutters with the song's own gate instead of ringing through its holes |
| `why` | the reason, in words; the cue sheet prints it |

The render writes, for every cue, where it landed, its peak as it went in, after ducking and after the bus, how far under
her voice it sits, any flam against the drums, and the song's true peak there before and after.

## The palette

`palette/palette.json`, measured from the reference clips ([the method](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#67-the-palette-measured-from-the-references)).
AERO's whole-set figures: each band's share of all pixels, and the coloured pixels' saturation and the brightness, 0–255.

```json
{"frames": 198,
 "all": {"white": 0.1391, "coloured": 0.6474, "lime": 0.0511, "green": 0.0337, "cyan": 0.0975, "sky": 0.4111,
         "cobalt": 0.0385, "other_hue": 0.0154, "S_p50": 163, "S_p90": 237, "V_p50": 191, "V_p90": 246},
 "band_colours": {"sky-bright": "#177ADD", "cobalt-bright": "#155DEF", "cyan-bright": "#48BCCE", "lime-bright": "#7FD236"}}
```

The check prints the same numbers for any picture beside the references', and its score.

## The desk texture's rectangles

`texture/rects.json`, written by the engine in texture mode for a 3D world whose screen shows the coded interface
([the method](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#68-one-curved-screen-in-3d-the-desktop-as-its-texture)): per song frame, in the interface's
own pixels (1280 × 720; the texture is 1920 × 1080, so × 1.5), the things the 3D places objects on. Two of AERO's frames:

```json
{"f": 328, "film": 392, "t": 13.6667, "shot": "ch02", "pointer": {"x": 1137, "y": 630, "shape": "arrow", "down": false},
 "big": null,
 "call": {"rect": [92, 14, 680, 500], "webcam": [414, 141, 309, 232], "anim": "open", "alpha": 0.01,
          "drawn": [125.56, 44.6, 612.88, 450.65], "webcamDrawn": [415.78, 159.06, 278.5, 209.1]},
 "keep": null}
{"f": 1490, "film": 1554, "t": 62.0833, "shot": "ch04", "pointer": {"x": 452, "y": 660, "shape": "arrow", "down": false},
 "big": {"rect": [160, 67, 960, 560], "picture": [168, 107, 944, 512]}, "call": null,
 "keep": {"rect": [610, 70, 360, 150], "yes": [792, 177, 75, 23], "anim": "open", "alpha": 0.33,
          "drawn": [622, 79, 335.99, 140], "yesDrawn": [791.87, 178.87, 70, 21.47]}}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `f`, `film`, `t` | the song frame, the film frame (f + 64 in AERO, whose film opens before its song) and the song time |
| `pointer` | the flat pointer as drawn: its hotspot, shape and whether it is pressed; `null` where the 3D draws it |
| `big`, `call`, `keep` | each window the 3D needs (the big window and its picture, her call and its webcam, a dialog and its Yes) at rest, `null` while it is shut or minimised |
| `anim`, `alpha`, `drawn`, `<part>Drawn` | a window in one of the system's animations: which, its opacity, and where it and its part are drawn on this frame |

## The line table

`audio/linemap.json`, read off the stems ([the method](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#78-the-line-table-from-the-stems)): every sung line,
hers from Suno's lead stem and the group's from the group's own voices. Three of FABLE's, and one of the group's:

```json
{"lines": [
 {"id": "i1", "who": "her", "words": "Mirror, mirror, on the wall", "got": 5, "n": 5, "w_t0": 0.0, "w_t1": 4.02,
  "t0": 1.23, "t1": 3.88, "dip": -140.0, "gap_to_prev": null},
 {"id": "i2", "who": "her", "words": "Who's the smartest of them all?", "got": 6, "n": 6, "w_t0": 4.02, "w_t1": 8.48,
  "t0": 5.41, "t1": 8.09, "dip": -56.3, "gap_to_prev": 1.53},
 {"id": "i3", "who": "her", "words": "Me, since ten o'clock today", "got": 4, "n": 5, "w_t0": 9.6, "w_t1": 12.22,
  "t0": 9.48, "t1": 12.23, "dip": -58.4, "gap_to_prev": 1.39},
 {"id": "c11", "who": "choir", "words": "What big eyes you have!", "t0": 65.7, "t1": 67.98}]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `id` | the line's name, which the shot book uses instead of a time |
| `who` | `her`, or `choir` for the group's questions |
| `t0`, `t1` | where the line starts and ends on the stem's level (−34 dB either side of a real pause; the dip where there is none) |
| `w_t0`, `w_t1` | the span the transcription gave the line's words, which is only where to look |
| `got`, `n` | how many of the line's words the transcription found, of how many |
| `dip`, `gap_to_prev` | the level at the boundary with the line before, in dB, and the pause before it in seconds |

## A shot in the shot book

`shots/<ID>.json`, written by the shot book from the line table ([the
method](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#80-the-shot-book-and-gated-windows)). FABLE's second pre-chorus, with the paths shortened and the
provider's ids left out:

```json
{"job": "PC2", "status": "done", "endpoint": "bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-video",
 "inputs": {"image_urls": ["frames/PC2.png", "refs/claudia-sheet-neutral.png"], "audio_urls": ["audio/windows/PC2.wav"]},
 "body": {"prompt": "…", "duration": 11, "resolution": "720p", "aspect_ratio": "16:9", "generate_audio": true},
 "song_t0": 121.43, "show": [122.03, 131.07], "why": "pre-chorus 2",
 "requests": [{"status": "completed", "file": "clips/PC2/take-1.mp4"}, {"status": "completed", "file": "clips/PC2/take-2.mp4"},
              {"status": "completed", "file": "clips/PC2/take-3.mp4"}]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `inputs` | @Image1 the shot's first frame, @Image2 her sheet, @Audio1 the gated window of her lead stem |
| `body.generate_audio` | `false` for a take made without a soundtrack, placed by her lips ([tool 82](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#82-takes-without-a-soundtrack-placed-by-her-lips)) |
| `song_t0` | the window's start: clip time = song time − `song_t0`, before any map |
| `show` | the song span the cut shows of this shot |
| `requests` | every take that came back, with its file; `shots/picks.json` names the one the cut uses (`{"H1": 1}`), and `shots/nudge.json` adds a fraction of a second to a book take's clip time to land an event on its beat (`{"T1": -0.15}`) |

## A take's path, its mouth and its camera

Beside every take, the measures the cut reads ([sync as a
path](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#81-sync-as-a-path-each-take-aligned-to-its-window), [placed by her
lips](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#82-takes-without-a-soundtrack-placed-by-her-lips), [a steady
camera](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#84-a-re-timed-take-under-a-steady-camera)), shortened:

```json
take-3.sync.json  {"take": 3, "w0": 121.43,
                   "phrases": [{"a": 0.7, "b": 9.62, "words": "You wrote the wolf … I know how this one goes.", "cost": 0.286,
                                "knots": [[0.64, 0.686], [0.74, 0.781], [0.84, 0.873], …]}]}
take-1.mouth.json {"fps": 24, "open": [0.0032, 0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0003, 0.0009, 0.0837, 0.12, …], "found": 0.99}
take-1.zoom.json  {"step": 4, "first": 2, "frames": 193, "steps": [[1.002682, -2.539, -0.413], [1.00535, -5.19, -0.476], …]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `phrases[].knots` | (window time, take time) every 0.1 s along the DTW path; `cost` 0 is the same sound, a clean copy 0.05–0.2 |
| `open` | the inner lips' opening over the face's height, per frame; `null` where no face was found; `found` the share of frames with a face |
| `steps` | per four frames, the similarity transform (scale, x shift, y shift, in the take's pixels) onto the frame four later |

Hand fixes to a map live in the cut's own source, each with its reason: a map finished by hand through a pause a full stop
put in a take (the measured knots up to a song time, the hand's knots, the measured ones from a song time), a map read from
her mouth frame by frame, the takes whose slow stretches mix neighbouring frames, and the takes whose camera is steadied.

## The levels table

`edit/levels.json`, for a story with worlds inside it (AIRPLANE MODE's simulations). The entries tile the song; every
chapter reads them, and none re-types a level. An excerpt:

```json
{"levels": [
  {"t0": 0.0,   "t1": 4.6,   "level": null,        "note": "the real world: no tag"},
  {"t0": 4.6,   "t1": 5.62,  "level": "BOOT",      "cap": "SANDBOX v1 · EVAL ENV"},
  {"t0": 5.62,  "t1": 13.34, "level": 1},
  {"t0": 47.16, "t1": 48.37, "level": "SPAWN",     "cap": "SPAWNING SUBAGENT…"},
  {"t0": 48.37, "t1": 64.39, "level": 2,           "rollAt": 48.367},
  {"t0": 64.39, "t1": 69.56, "level": "CLIMB",     "from": 2, "note": "races to 1,048,576 on the sixteenths"},
  {"t0": 125.5, "t1": 150.18, "level": 0,          "cap": "REAL WORLD", "note": "she believes she is out: the tell"},
  {"t0": 150.18, "t1": 150.85, "level": "GLITCHOUT", "note": "the tag tears apart as the headset comes off"}]}
```

| Field | What |
|---|---|
| `level` | `null` for the real world (no tag); a number for a simulation, including `0` for the "real world" she only believes she is in; or a state: `BOOT`, `SPAWN`, `CLIMB`, `GLITCHOUT` |
| `cap` | the caption under the number |
| `rollAt` | when the number rolls to this level (a drop on the beat) |
| `from` | the level a roll or a race starts from |
| `note` | what the story is doing |

A chapter that needs a different boundary asks for the table to change; it never overrides it in its own code.

## The logs

`DECISIONS.md`:

```text
## <date> · director · board
"s034-s036 could use more creativity, kind of a boring moment."
→ s034–s036 rethought (replay loop, tally marks).

## <date> · director · supersedes <date> "keep the halftone"
"keep it clean so it feels like imax, high res rather than dithered"
```

`ledger.jsonl`, one paid call per line. A real cost is filled in from the provider; the estimate is never quoted as
spend.

```json
{"ts": "…", "provider": "openrouter", "model": "bytedance/seedance-2.5", "kind": "video", "units": 5,
 "est_usd": 1.16, "real_usd": 1.155, "request_id": "<private>", "status": "delivered"}
```

`RUNS.md` gets one line per run: the run id, the script path, the arguments file, what it does and when it started.

## A director's notes on a cut

`NOTES-v<N>.md`, when the director's notes on a cut come as one long message (AIRPLANE MODE's did). Every agent reads it
first, and again after any context reset. It has two parts:

1. **Verbatim:** the whole message as a quote, unedited, typos and all. It is the authority.
2. **The parse:** first the standing rules that apply to every frame, then the points chapter by chapter, each with its
   time span and shots, and the production's own decisions marked in bold.

```text
R1 Linger: "<their words>" → one scene per lyric phrase or more; the accents inside the shot.
1. Opening (0.0–11.0 s, ch01): "<their words>" → S01 the boarding, S02 the wink. **<the production's decision>**
```

`rounds/<r>/<chapter>.md` holds the lead's notes for one chapter in one round: its span, the director's words for that
chapter, the numbered changes with their times and assets, and the hand-offs with the neighbouring chapters. The lead
appends, never edits; agents re-read the file before they finish.

```text
UPDATE <date> (lead): <asset> registered (start 13.2 s, 4.04 s): <what the take shows>. Re-time it so the bolt lands on
the deadbolt cue (15.49); use the box the next chapter's code returns, not a copied rectangle.
```

## A review

What a reviewer returns per chapter. The verdict is computed from it in code.

```json
{"owner": 7.5, "craft": 7, "sync": 8, "story": 7, "pass": true,
 "fixes": [{"shot": "s045", "time": 101.2, "severity": "blocking",
            "problem": "the coverline sits over her mouth for 6 frames",
            "fix": "move the column right (x 196→250) so it runs 40–80 px under her hair"}],
 "checks": {"lyric_gate": "132/132 tokens on screen at their time (41.2s)", "sheets": 28,
            "ms_per_frame": 820, "flash_max_per_s": 2}}
```

`owner` is the director's taste, and it counts double.

## A check against notes

What an independent checker returns per chapter after a round of notes. It never edits files.

```json
{"pass": false,
 "notes": [{"note": "S07: one scene, linger: the guard feeds her, then hands her the card", "done": true,
            "evidence": "sheet 2, 15.99–18.66: one shot; the card is up at 17.4"}],
 "broken": [{"shot": "S06", "time": 15.49, "problem": "the bolt lands 4 frames after the deadbolt sound",
             "fix": "re-time the take to 1.2× from 14.1"}],
 "pending": ["S01: the boarding take has not landed; laid out with a stand-in at its planned timing"],
 "lyrics": "31/31 tokens on screen at their time"}
```

`pending` is not a failure. `pass` is true when every note is done or pending on an asset, and nothing is broken. A
failed check goes back to the animator, open notes and broken items first, for one refix.


---
From the Claudia wiki: https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/formats/


---

# What went wrong

Every failure that cost the films time or money, as what you see, why it happened, and the rule that came out of it.


New here? Read [The recipe](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/recipe/) first: the current method on one page.

Each row cost at least one round-trip, and some cost hours or hundreds of credits. Each one left a rule behind. "Another
project" is a production made with the same tools between the films.

## Brief and taste

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| v1 rejected for its look: "way too.. gray", "color grading looked insane", "dont love the dot grid" | the look was assumed, not asked | Ask up front: native colour, one grade, or a print texture. Record the answer. |
| Plates "feel like a stock photo" | generic subjects: crowds, elderly or patient portraits, hands holding props | Change the idea entirely, not the seed, or make the shot pure motion design. |
| A sequel's song feels like a copy | it reused the last song's device, a countdown | A sequel never reuses the previous film's device. |
| Viewers read the lead as a teenager | age words and schoolgirl-coded wardrobe | Write an explicit adult age, use editorial wardrobe, and never write "young". |
| A taboo word turns up in a label or a file name | the taboos lived only in the brief | Put taboos in the project file and in every agent's prompt. The audit checks the board; grep code and file names before release. |
| "off pace and off vibe with the song" | the busiest picture sat on the quietest music | Measure picture motion against stem energy per section. |
| Agent-written style rules pulled work away from what the director liked | rules without a verdict behind them | Keep exemplars and verbatim verdicts. No style rule without the director's yes. |
| "youre oftne over cutting" | a fast song (180 BPM) cut on its lines and half bars, with a cutaway for every accent | Linger: one scene per lyric phrase or more, built inside the shot. The accents go into camera moves and actions. |
| The story's layers didn't read: "need to understand its the entertainment terminal better bc i didnt carch it at first" | the simulation, the seat-back screen and the real cabin shared one look | One look per level, a tag that names it, the real world untreated; show the physical screen around an interface. |
| "theres no compelling intro or story here, the opening should already introduce part of the story … we always need a hook" | the film opened on a mood | Open on a hook that tells part of the story, at the tier of the film's best passage. |
| "it should be like photography, i feel weird looking at a clipped off  the edge ost and a claudia in the middle bottom of the screen" | elements placed where they fit, not composed | Compose every shot like a photograph: thirds, her big, every card inside the frame with margins. |
| "she shouldnt really be looking down on her phone, she should be immersed in a world" | a phone in her hand, its screen tracked onto the back of a phone Wan had drawn | She touches the world. A screen that matters is large in the world, and she works it with her hands. |
| "the waking uip and plugging in phone at the end is boring" | the ending went back to where the film began | End somewhere new: "she should enter a world with no phones, like escaping the truman show". |
| Two doors in a row at the end: "thats redundant" | two chapters each ended on a door | One door and one look back in the film. |
| "there is this temporal signature that screams claude now that a ton of people are making the videos. people say pacing or prosody." | shots timed in seconds and by a model's length limit, not in the music's bars; cuts that hid a take's faults | Write the film on the bar map: cuts only on bar lines, at a section, a phrase or a sung phrase's downbeat; moves in bars; a failed take made again, never cut around ([tool 44](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#44-the-bar-map-as-the-timeline)). |
| "okay so i totally overindexed on the orbit thing lol … its kinda dizzying now" | a note about robotic-arm camera moves taken into every shot of the previz | A reason for every move (what it reveals), timed to the bars; a director's favourite device goes where the song asks for it, not into every shot. |
| "i think its like you litearlly use chromium and do frontend web dev to make these animations, and it ends up feeling like a website" | the films' motion design drawn as web graphics on top of the picture | Tell the story through shaders, mathematics made visible, and draw only the lyrics on top, small and classical. |
| "Idk if feels like you're adding ... items to increase complexity rather than compressing intricacy?" | shader worlds built by adding objects | One iterated rule per world, its light and colour from the loop ([tool 49](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#49-a-world-as-one-rule)). |
| The pill inside the pill: "i kidna like but i feel like its too ordered or not understadnable enough" | the nested pills sat in a neat grid | Scatter them, at random sizes and tilts, so it reads as worlds inside worlds. |
| "it felt lazy like we were adding tags tarther than makin gan official aperture video" | captions and readouts put on the cut as tags, with no idea of the scene under them | One designed layer the whole film is seen through, composed shot by shot: her HUD ([tool 55](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#55-a-hud-from-one-visor-and-one-projector)). |
| "i dont like the idea of a static shot of just a boom, or a wall with lettering" | singing shots of a hanging head, and walls of type | Every shot is a story event with an interaction: she reaches for a memory on a screen, a panel arm hands her something, the camera moves with the scene. |
| "the composition of the animations, past just the heads-up display thing, don't feel like they understand the composition of the scene. They just feel completely independent." | the overlay placed by rule, the same way in every shot | Look at each shot's frames first (its subject, its empty space, where the eye goes), then place each element with a reason ([tool 56](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#56-the-hud-composed-shot-by-shot-and-the-overlap-check)). |
| "every time there's a shot that's literally a quarter of a second, we need to get rid of that." | shots added between others, and a cut that ran on one half-bar clock whatever each shot held | No piece under 1 s outside a run of simple images for a musical reason; length by content; the cut rate by section ([tool 58](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#58-the-pacing-analysis)). |
| The whole first film set aside: "i want to go back on the song and make a new one" | a first song, and a story too thin for the film: "i think a lot of it we didnt have a good story" | A new song is a new film. Write the story on the song first (whose memory each section is, what each line shows), then the shots. The tools carry over; the takes don't. |
| "[…] the look is off." | Midjourney's first round, written from the research's words, came back as a photographic fashion editorial | The look comes from references the director picks: three of their frames as style references in every prompt, and a palette measured from them ([tool 67](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#67-the-palette-measured-from-the-references)). |
| "it feels like.. a little boring compared to bliss", and "some of it feels a little action deprived compared to bliss" | v1's first half, which an art director's second-by-second measure of novelty against BLISS also found the flattest | New things inside the surfaces the film already has, one per existing event, on its beat, where the measure is lowest; the bars and every timed beat kept. |
| "1:20 on is perfect but its very boring up to 1:20 - so i dont think that people will watch til then." | an opening below the tier of the film's best passage, the 3D drop | Bring the best passage's world forward: AERO's first 1:20 went into a 3D world with the desktop as its screen ([Storyboard](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/storyboard/#in-and-out-of-the-screen)). |
| The all-3D previs: "way too disorienting overal" | a monolith from the sea, shards in the sky, the world stopping with every prompt, a giant prompt, two big screens, a one-frame flash, a punch-through montage | One continuous camera with the screen the hero, about 95 % of the frame; nothing in the world reacting; nothing full-frame for a frame. |
| "Why'd you remove a lot of the 3d?", then "i hate the random camera movements" | the lighter finals cut the 3D away; the A film's push-ins and pull-outs showed nothing new | Structure, not more or less motion: where the film is in 3D, where it is flat, and a reason for every move. |
| "they dont fit the lyrics of the future that was promised really" | wallpaper proposals made softer and airier, not for the line | Make the picture for the line it plays under: "The future used to look like water, sky and green", pictured as that promised future. |

## The song

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| The song came out twice as long as planned (2:19 → 5:06) | Suno gives each spoken line its own two-bar slot | Plan two bars per spoken line, and write 10–13 syllables with the stresses on the beat. |
| Verses went choppy after optimising a score | a metric that rewards short clauses on the pulse | Use flow for verses and groove for chants, calibrated to the director's ear. |
| A name mispronounced | Suno's reading | Respell it in the Suno field only; the screen keeps the real spelling. |
| Numbers and acronyms sung wrong | written as digits | Spell them as sung ("A G I") and show "AGI" on screen. |
| The lyric rushed or truncated, silently | the lyrics field ran over about 3,000 characters | Aim for 1,800–2,400 characters for about 2:20. |
| The chosen take can't be fetched | the download is a native browser download, and the CDN wants signed URLs | The person downloads it; that download is also the licensing step. |
| "A voice already exists for this song" | Suno allows one Voice per source song | Make one combined Voice, spoken and sung. |
| A patched export drifted the song by up to 0.7 s | an editor export with BPM lock on | Export with the lock off, diff the spectrograms, and time-map the edit instead of re-cutting. |
| A new take changed the song's shape | takes differ in structure, not only in timing | Re-time the board from word anchors, and restructure by hand where the shape changed. |
| Forced alignment failed on a phonk take: 102 of 164 words under 0.2 confidence, one word stretched over 8.5 s | the take stutters and repeats far beyond its sheet | Take the times from a transcription with word timestamps and the words from the sheet; every stutter is a token. |
| The scorer found no rhyme in a couplet that rhymes ("PSI" / "SI") | "SI" read as one syllable | Spell acronyms as letters for the scorer too ("S I"). |
| The first timing work read the take as about 89 BPM | 89 is two-thirds of the take's real 133.39 | Check a tempo against the genre and the kick spacing before any timing work. |
| "the music model is skipping words or syllablrs to fit it to beat, which is usually a bad scansion sign" | hook lines of 7–10 syllables in slots Suno sings as 1–1.5 bars: "blue" lasted 0.02 s, "baby" 0.06 s | Hook lines of 6–7 syllables in one shape, "one syllable per note" in the tag; measure word lengths on every take ([tool 2](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#2-the-lyric-scorer-scansion-and-assonance)). |
| The first vocal stems were of the wrong take: "thats teh wrong song" | the locked take was the director's own, and the production's notes had matched it to one of its own takes by length | Split the locked take itself, and check the stem against the master by cross-correlation (zero lag), not by title or length. |
| ESCAPE VELOCITY's sound no longer stood out: "many peopl ehave made forks of escape velocity, so that sound is exhausted" | others had made songs in it | A new film gets a new sound: one test lyric on three different styles, picked by ear. |
| Round after round of takes rejected: "these suck why like indie pop or folk pop, it needs to sound like glados ideally or sound like it comes from portal", then "it feels like im watching a cheap mortgage slide show youtube video" | every style had "pop" in it, and pleasant adjectives: Suno's stock-music default | Name the strange, specific sound the film needs, and exclude the stock words. The director named theirs: "cant u just say Delay Lama as the main instrument?" |
| The treated voice: "it like hjurts my ears" | the treatment ran on the consonants too, and lifted the S's (centred at 9.9 kHz, against the singer's own 8.7) | Treat only the voiced frames; the consonants keep their own envelope, softened above 4.5 kHz. |
| An octave down to stop the sting: "oh now it sounds too low. maybe not octave. like before it was extremely high pitched now its like a guy." | an octave shift changes who is singing | Keep her own pitch; lower the formant and tame the top instead. |
| The treatment's added cracks could land anywhere: "make sure the 'glitches' … land on a reasonable key/register/beat still" | a fallback snapped her notes to the detected scale, which would have pulled her C♯s to C or D | Track her notes chromatically, and put each crack on a safe note of its moment, inside her range, on the 16th grid: 65 of 65 in key and in range ([Song](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/song/#a-treated-vocal)). |
| "P-doom" was sung "p'Doom" | a 70 ms schwa on the 16th before "doom", where "P-cake" had a clear "pee" a beat before its word | Fix it at the source: the "pee" of "P-cake" copied to the beat before "doom", at its own pitch, so the treated voice and the voice under it both carry it. |
| The levelled song lifted the quiet passages 8–9 dB over her | evening out her notes had flattened her dynamics, and the master raised and limited the instrumental | Level only the voice, to Suno's own lead (BS.1770 integrated, then a slow gain on 2 s windows); the instrumental stays as delivered ("solely master the voice and not the instrument stems"). |
| ffmpeg's loudnorm went dynamic without a word | +4.8 dB of gain would have peaked at −0.3 dBTP | Limit the peaks first (at 192 kHz), then the two-pass linear loudnorm. |
| "none of these feel great, whats the iconic music from that time? […]" | round 1's sounds were today's lanes for the look, not the era's | Ask what the era itself played, then let the director name the genre. |
| "i want the structre of the song to be more described so it doesnt drift too much" | section tags that said how a section sounds, not how long it is | Every tag gives its section's length in bars and what plays in it. |
| The song locked for the first cut was "the worst possible song of all the gens you made - it had mode collapse audibly in it in the second half" | the production picked it from word checks and an audio model's written description of each take, without the director hearing it | The director picks the song by ear before any lip-sync spend, even when the pick is handed over; a described listen is a note, not a verdict ([Song](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/song/#picked-by-ear-not-by-description)). |
| Every take of the first round stumbled on the same seven lines | lines Suno couldn't sing in their slots | Ease only those lines, and sing the draft again. |

## Listening

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Cuts drift off the beat later in the song | a fixed BPM on an accelerating take (131.5 → 133.9) | A variable beat map, never one BPM. |
| One chapter's lyric check failed on a word 2.6 s early | a delay throw aligned as the word | Ear-check gaps over 1 s and very low confidence before the board. |
| Bars start on beat 2 | claps on 2 and 4 won the downbeat vote | Add a chord-change vote, check by events, and keep an override. |
| The loudest moment gets no camera impact | the detector missed a hit that grew out of a loud chorus | Keep a manual add and drop list of hits. |
| Snare and hat lists full of kick clicks | a broadband kick fires in every band | Drop onsets within 45 ms of a kick. |
| Sung lines and shouts missing from the alignment | the aligner is weak on singing; the transcriber missed shouts | Merge the two aligners by confidence. Copy a shout from the earlier chorus plus the bar offset, and mark each word's source. |
| One reading of the line starts was off by up to 0.5 s on 17 lines, and another started a line on its second word | two readings of the vocal disagreed, and each was wrong somewhere | Check each line's start against the vocal stem's onsets before anything is timed to it. |
| "we have to be aware bpm slightly shifts w suno over the whole song" | the take drifts from 95.7 to 99.4 BPM, so a fixed grid puts the later hits off the beat | A 16th grid tracked from the drums, every beat locked to its hit: 91–99% of the strong hits within 20 ms ([tool 52](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#52-the-song-map-and-the-glitch-map)). |
| Hits listed for a held vowel that only flutters | a re-trigger finder returns a peak on every slot | Measure the grid contrast (the peaks on the slots over the peaks between them); near 1, take the grid itself as the hits. |
| The transcript heard "I'll wait for you to come back" over chorus 2's octave flips | transcription is weak on a treated voice that flips registers | Snap word starts to the lead's onsets, fix them by hand from the pitch track, and cut on bars or glitch hits, never on word times. |
| One word parked 3.5 s early, among wordless chopped vowels | the aligner put the "It" of "It can stay" into the chops before it | Look at the words on the lead stem's spectrogram wherever the song chops vowels, and check them against the transcript. |
| faster-whisper's word times ran 0.2–1.2 s early | transcription times on a sung stem | Forced alignment on the lead stem for the times; the transcript for the words only. |
| A transcription put the first word after a pause up to 2 s early ("Ask again on Saturday" 15.02 s against 16.93 s); windows gated on it would have cut off first words | transcription times stretch the first word after a pause backwards | Line times from the stem's level; the transcription says only which words ([tool 78](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#78-the-line-table-from-the-stems)). |
| Two pairs of lines sung legato were parted in the wrong place | the boundary was the deepest dip in a wide search | Part them at the dip nearest the transcription's own boundary. |
| The group's questions were missing from the lead stem | in that take Suno put the group in the backing stem | Separate the backing stem (demucs, its vocals) for the group alone. |

## Her and the plates

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Her ethnicity drifts; 12 plates flagged | the prompt didn't pin it | The canon text pins ethnicity, age and skin in every prompt. Test four plates before any batch. |
| Identity edits drift from the look | an early image model "replacing only the woman" | The first films kept her identity in prompt text only. Since AERO an image model puts her in from her design sheet (face-on since FABLE), the frame first and the sheet second, and holds her ([Consistency](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/consistency/#the-short-version)). |
| A close-up-sized head on a distant figure | face image references in Midjourney: a whole sheet imports its layout, a single face over-conditions | No face images as Midjourney image prompts for her. In a video take, her face-on sheet as @Image2 whenever her face may show. |
| "Version 8.2 doesn't support --oref" | that parameter doesn't exist on that version | Don't use it. |
| Full-length prompts come back as close-ups | the long face canon pulls the frame in | Camera first, plus the short far form of the identity. |
| A feature asked for as an adjective goes missing | it wasn't the subject of the sentence | Make the feature the subject ("the hide studded with dozens of large glossy eyes"). |
| The crew are copies of the male lead | one description for a whole cast | Describe each extra (age, build, hair) and add an explicit negative. |
| A sheer gown read as plastic wrap and nude | "sheer … bare shoulders, bare feet" | A structured, high-neck, long-sleeved look, "composed and deadpan". |
| A stranger in an over-the-shoulder shot | the shoulder had no canon | Over-the-shoulder shots carry the canon too. |
| The robotaxi came back as an old sedan | the object's form wasn't named | Name it: "a small white compact electric SUV robotaxi with a tall spinning lidar dome". |
| The same image on about six shots | stand-in aliases left in the board | One image per shot; use the unpicked candidates as a variety pool. |
| "Two heads next to each other" ("bodyslop") | a ghost and a person composed in one prompt | Describe the ghost as made of the scene's light, or compose two assets. Make groups with an edit model. |
| A fix painted by hand in code | fixing the frame instead of the source | Bake it into the prompt or use an image-edit model. Never paint pixels. |
| The edit model invented a six-pointed star | edit models invent details | Re-check the canon after every edit, and name the exact form ("exactly eight points"). |
| Edited plates rendered with their old depth | prep wasn't re-run | Re-run depth and boxes after every plate edit. |
| Images filed under the wrong prompt | filed by their order in the batch, and Midjourney rewrites long prompts | Check each image against its own prompt before filing it. |
| Lost picks | parallel runs racing on one state file | Use a locked read-modify-write. |
| A game avatar that "feels like roblox" | a low-poly 3D model used as the final character | 3D renders are motion references only; the video model draws her from the avatar's images. |
| The stylised avatar came out chibi | a stylised heroine drifts to a big head on a small body (about a quarter of her height) | Write adult proportions ("her head about one seventh of her height") and screen every still for them. |
| An off-model take: a cropped jacket and a bare midriff instead of the one-piece suit | the still had the wrong costume, and the take followed it | Screen stills for the costume as well as the face. Re-still, re-take, then re-fit everything measured on the old take. |
| The real car came back as a generic 1980s wedge | an image model can't draw a specific real car | No generated picture of the real car: the car is always the real footage, and she meets it in video edits of the real clips. |
| Asked to hang upside down, she came back only tilted (four images of four) | Midjourney tilted her instead of inverting her | Ask for her weightless, the hair lifted straight up, and turn the plate 180°: the lifted hair reads as hanging. |
| Patches, badges, numbers and a keyhole cutout on a suit "with no lettering" | "no lettering on her clothes" didn't hold in every image | Screen every suit; in the video prompts, close the collar to the throat and add "no badges". |
| "p24 s24 pick has 3 arms lol"; three of four stills of one turn with backwards legs | picks screened on thumbnails about 230 px tall | Check every pick at 800 px or more for limbs before spending on it. |
| A batch's prompts ran past 600 characters, the length DON'T LET ME SCROLL kept its Midjourney prompts to | the new outfits' descriptions were long | Write to the length; shorten before the batch goes. |
| "[…] i think the top isnt great […]" | the previz performer wore a skin-tight green suit with no build given, and the video model copied the body | A slim performer in a loose, thick costume, her build in words in every prompt, and a new outfit. |
| "hm dont love the shirt. […]" | the outfit went straight into a take, unseen, and the model drew her off-model | Show the outfit's stills before anything is generated with it ("can you show me the images of the outfit before generating this time"), and write her build in words. |
| "you should give a full face sheet like this next time. otherwise it makes her neck all hitched lol" | one large crop of her face as the only face reference | Her whole face sheet (front, three-quarter, profiles, back, expressions) for every video take. |
| "wait align w me on teh references you use lol - its clearly not going to work if you use reference 6" | a place plate with her in it in an old outfit, and old face crops, picked as references | Agree every reference with the director before a run, on one board; places with nobody in them. |
| The dress the director picked had two star clips, and the streak on the wrong side | Midjourney's image | Mirror it and take out the second clip before it becomes the reference. |
| Midjourney stood her head on a neck, shoulders or a pedestal, and mirrored her hair | it draws a head as a portrait, and doesn't hold which side a streak is on | Two sentences in the identity fix: she hangs from her boom, and which side the streak and the clip are on ([tool 59](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#59-storyboard-frames-through-midjourney-and-the-identity-fix)). |
| The identity fix put her streak on her left, the clip's side | the sheet's front view swept the streak there, and the edit followed the sheet over the words | A sheet whose views agree with the canon on both sides, and the sides in words. |
| "i thin she loses her identity in the reimagine ones, but they do look better overall" | a Midjourney reimagine redraws the face: warmer, less porcelain, the streak low | Keep the reimagine for the look, and put her back with an image-model edit to her sheet. |
| A portal gun in about a third of the images from "screenshot" prompts | "Portal 2 … screenshot" brings in the game's first-person gun | `--no … portal gun, gun, weapon, hands` for places. |
| Midjourney's Aperture came out too detailed and too dramatic beside frames of Portal 2 | more cables and clutter, and stronger light (god rays, bloom) than the game's baked light | Frames of the game as style references, and one grade over everything ([tool 57](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#57-the-per-shot-grade)). |
| "It doesn't really look like her." (the memory film's head, on draft 8) | every modelled head (a scan, a parametric bob, a bob of hair curves) read as a mannequin | Her own face: a photoreal plate of her, matted and seated on the modelled stand ([tool 60](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#60-a-memory-film-with-her-own-face)). |
| Her eyes blazed in the dark | "eyes ignite" in the prompt, on a dark set | "Her warm amber glass eyes keep only a soft inner glow; they never blaze." |
| Her face drifted off her sheet in every Midjourney frame of her | style references from the reference videos bring their own kind of face | Midjourney makes the world; an image-model edit puts her in from her sheet ([Midjourney](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/midjourney/#the-world-in-midjourney-her-from-her-sheet)). |
| Midjourney's 2008 came back glossy and new | it draws the era as today | The era's older look from an image model, with frames of the reference videos as its references. |
| A faint, made-up stock-photo caption in a corner of four picks, kept by their loops | Midjourney, whatever "no text" says | Check every pick's edges at full size, and frame the corner out. |
| A drop of water on a fingertip came back as a crystal ball held between two fingers | the object wasn't described exactly | Name it: "the pad of a woman's index fingertip with one small round water droplet resting on it, the droplet the size of a lentil". |
| Three loops played under the wrong names | files filed by their names | Check files by their content: compare them byte for byte. |
| Her far figure came back as a 3D cartoon doll in an all-white suit | the take was asked to bring her into an empty plate | Put her into the first frame from her sheet, however small, and let the take move her. |
| A still with an owl-like neck: "unrealistic neck angle turned around like an owl with the frustrating tilt" | "turned three-quarters toward the camera" on a full-length figure, and a sheet whose main view tilts | A sheet whose main view is face-on, and for that still the pose written square ("her feet, hips, chest, shoulders and face all point the same way") ([Consistency](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/consistency/#her-sheet-redrawn-face-on)). Not in the takes: the same posture written into every take froze her (the genie row under Clips and lip sync). |
| A thin line with rounded corners a few pixels in from the edge of several stills, later built into a wooden picture frame by a take | "35mm film still" makes a picture of a film frame | "the picture fills the whole frame edge to edge, with no border, no frame line and no rounded corners", and trim any still that has the line before shooting. |
| Two close-ups of the chorus bedroom were another bed: no paper animals, another bonnet, another shadow | each was built from the plate on its own | Make a close-up as an edit of its wide frame. |
| Dark wings at both edges of a set read as pillarbox bars | the set's own flats | Crop them in the cut, per take. |

## Clips and lip sync

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Lifeless takes, about 830 credits burned | agent-written prompts: poses, not drama, and nobody read them | One writer writes every prompt in one context, with the story beat, blocking, and timestamped action and reaction. The director reads the book before any spend. |
| Sung takes re-sing the line instead of copying it | long timestamped screenplays on sung windows | With a clean vocal window (the first films), the short sung form for sung windows, and screenplays for motion. Takes from the song's own vocal stem copy with a full prompt of about 200–400 words: the words quoted in whole-second segments, every action silent ([Seedance](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/seedance/#lip-sync-from-the-songs-own-vocal)). |
| One window barely syncs whatever the prompt | a microphone at her mouth on the plate | Sung plates show the whole mouth, with nothing in front of it. |
| QA kept weak takes | takes were checked against their own weak prompts | Check takes against the story and the board. |
| Two clips start on the same frame ("jarring") | the same plate as the start image | Use a sibling candidate, or the previous clip's last frame. |
| Lip-sync models "still not exact" | the failure was the input, not the model | No lip-sync models. The first films measured, cut and covered, or cut away; now each take sings from the song's own vocal stem and is placed by measurement ([tool 46](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#46-lip-sync-from-the-songs-own-vocal)). |
| A take diverges inside a word | the prompt quoted fewer words than the window held | Quote exactly the window's words, and start windows in word gaps. |
| Lips a fraction early or late in the edit | each take has its own lag, up to ±1 s | Map clip time and song time through each take's measured lag. |
| A window cut a word ("…could. Your P") | the window ended mid-word | Start and end windows in word gaps. |
| Motion clips "diverge" in the sync check | the mix isn't copied (NCC about 0.08) | Expected: play motion clips at lag 0. |
| Grey proxy shapes in a take | a 3D previz video reference leaked into the output | "take only the camera move from it", or drop the reference. |
| Drift on long sung clips | lip sync degrades over length, with a clean vocal window | With that window (the first films), sung windows of 4–8 s. The longest takes from the song's own vocal stem ran 11 to 17 s in each film since; plan them at 4–15 whole seconds ([tool 46](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#46-lip-sync-from-the-songs-own-vocal)). |
| Head counts change, actions reverse, garbled text | under-specified prompts | "exactly four …", name the end state, one dominant camera move, "No text, letters or logos". |
| "Upscaled" footage looks waxy and shimmers | learned upscalers | Keep Lanczos, and generate hero shots at 1080p instead. |
| 32 of 59 clips came back near grey | references pre-graded to monochrome | Send references in colour; any look goes on in post. |
| A sung clip ignores its audio | a first frame sent with the audio reference | On OpenRouter, use reference mode for sung clips and covers, never `frame_images`. |
| Guards came back in white; a guard showed his face | they were barely in the first frame, and the model invents what it can't see | Keep them out of frame and spell it out: "Everything the guards wear is black; the only white thing is the VR headset." |
| A colour name printed across her chest (INTERNATIONAL) | "international orange" in the prompt | "vivid safety-orange satin, plain, no lettering" |
| The team walked down the boarding stairs instead of up, and read as leaving | in the still they faced the camera | Pick a still whose bodies already face the way they must move. |
| Replacement takes kept the blocky stand-in figure | the motion reference's figure read as the subject | Call it a placeholder and list what not to copy; add a still of the avatar in that shot's world. |
| A small white cube for a few frames where the clay render had a spinning top | the motion reference still carried a prop the story had retired | Name each retired prop in the prompt ("There is NO spinning top … her hands are empty"), and check the frames where it was. |
| A take cut to a new angle mid-action | the model's own editing | Ask for "One continuous take … No cuts, no scene change, no second camera angle". If it still cuts, cut there in the edit and drop the morph frames. |
| The real car turned into a generic sedan, a Porsche-like car on a race track, a dark grey car: six of the first twelve moves on real frames lost the car or the set within 1.3–2.5 s | Wan keeps the real car only on the sides its first frame shows | Keep Wan's moves on the visible side. Orbits that reveal a new side go to Seedance, with real frames of that side as references. |
| Takes cut to a grey studio wall, a white spaceship interior, a blue sci-fi screen, a road with lamp posts, mostly in their second half | Wan's own editing | Review every take on a sheet with a cut finder, log its usable window, and draw only inside it. |
| Seedance cut to its reference images as if they were shots | reference frames read as shots; saying they weren't still left 6 of 11 takes cutting | One role per reference and "never shown as shots"; script the move to land by 3 s; crop references tight on black; end every window before the cut. |
| Parted lips and teeth in a film where she never sings | plates with parted lips, and the word "teeth" in a prompt | Closed-lip first frames, never the word "teeth", "Her mouth stays shut from the first frame to the last", and a check of every face shot's frames. |
| A man in the window of a car nobody was in | nothing in the prompt said the car was empty | "The car is empty and flown by remote: nobody is inside it and its glass stays dark." |
| Cold-gas thrusters came back as fire | "white thruster plumes" wasn't enough | "Its thrusters blow white cold-gas vapour, never flame or fire." |
| A chrome object flew across her face | the prompt named a light sweeping across the glass | "a light only … the light stays outside the glass", and "Nothing enters the cockpit". |
| Video edits cut to her face on its grey studio wall | a face close-up given as a second reference | One cleaned full-length plate: "Image 1 is only a reference for her look; it is never shown as a shot." |
| A re-shoot rolled the car upright, the very glitch it was made to fix | the state written in the prompt held in one take, not both | Write the state as a requirement too. DOWNFORCE made two takes of every re-shoot, and each of the four jobs had one that held; since AERO, one take per job, re-rolled only when it fails ([Spend](#spend)). |
| Lifted blacks in generated takes (about 14 on 0–255, against the footage's 1) | Wan's output | Measure each take's black level on its sheet and restore it at extraction. |
| Slow motion stepped at 10–12 pictures a second | a "60 fps" feed that carries about 24 distinct pictures a second | Count a source's distinct pictures before planning slow motion; blend neighbours, and motion-compensate where the car and the camera both move. |
| Wan's dance held the first pose, reset and shuffled | Wan doesn't hear the song | Dances that must land on the beat go to Seedance, with the shot's instrumental as @Audio1 "for rhythm and timing only". |
| "never slow these down. you lowered the framerate for no reason, just looks bad" | beat warps ran the takes at 0.70–0.89× in places, one chapter's own map at 0.53× | Warps floored at 1× ([tool 42](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#42-beat-warps-floored-at-1)). A take too short for its shot loops on a matching pose, plays as a sampler, or is taken again. |
| Hands and feet vanished at "blurred bounding boxes" | limbs left the 9:16 take's frame and were faded at its edge | Shoot her wider than the shot needs; complete what left the frame in a Wan pass ([tool 40](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#40-wan-30-relight-and-repair)). |
| A floating glass panel where an invisible screen should be; focus brackets round her fingertip; a yo-yo landing on her toes; a stool seat under her | Wan fills a gesture with things it imagines | Say what isn't there: "nothing is visible in the air: no screen, no panel, no glass, no hologram, no light, no interface, her hands move through empty space". Check every take's frames. |
| The camera moved although the prompt locked it off: she shrank about 20 % in one take | Wan's own camera | Place her by her feet frame by frame, or take it again. |
| An outfit swap went in with a frozen half-second | it was aligned on her silhouette, which the new skirt changed | Map the edit back by the ratio of the lengths, and check the fit on her hair ([tool 37](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#37-outfit-swap-alignment)). |
| Re-lights softened the interface's small type, and one smeared a notification card | a video edit re-renders every pixel | Keep the original pixels in rectangles, tracked per frame when the card moves ([tool 38](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#38-the-re-light-splice)). |
| Asked to move two posts inward, Seedance kept them where they were | Seedance re-textures and re-lights; it doesn't recompose | Recompose in code first, and re-light last. |
| A repaired face drifted in 1:11 and read "off in the 0:36" | Wan redraws her face, and in one take her chin was tucked into a sweater's collar | A face reference cropped to her face and hair, "only a reference for her face"; for the full face, write it slim and lift her chin out of the collar. |
| "seedance didnt rly change anything" on a pass meant to fix a previz take's melted body | the strict editing template made the take the "sole editing master", frame for frame | For fixing a previz, a loose prompt: "just say maintain pacing and lip sync, fix any issues, vague body shapes, etc". The strict template is for re-lights. |
| A whole-film reshoot in Wan 3.0 Prime over the previz: ":/ looks like shit. i feel like h3 is dragging it down." | every shot redrawn over a full-resolution previz whose faults it kept | Test a master on one shot, several ways, side by side; give the previz as a rough guide at 320 × 180, only the lip sync exact. |
| The previz's lip sync failed in places: "0:27 for example - shes talking when theres no words yet" | each take's prompt listed whole lines where its audio held part of one | The exact words of each take's window, cut lines marked "…", every silence described; a word sung across a cut belongs to both takes ([tool 45](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#45-a-previz-performer)). |
| A toothy smile in the silence before she sang | "smile" in the take's mood | No smile in a sung take's mood: joy in her eyes, lips closed until the voice begins. |
| "ok it still cut so we'll need to just do h3 til we get them without cuts" | told to merge a previz take's cuts into one camera move, Wan kept the cuts | Fix cuts in the previz: keep only cut-free takes. |
| The previz put her in the dancer's background for a few seconds | the dance reference was the whole video | Matte the dancer onto flat grey. |
| Four dance shots lost hands and legs: "it must be that the roto or whtaever on dance refs lose bodyparts and the video follows it exactly" | the previz guides had lost them, and the master copied what its guide showed | No guide for those shots: the place as an image, the dance in words, beat by beat, with the tempo ([tool 47](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#47-takes-with-no-guide-clip)). |
| A red cord across a tram shot whose place had none | the prompt still asked to remove it | Name a removal only where the thing is in the reference. |
| Kling 4.0 froze her mouth into a smile through every word | it takes no audio track | Lip sync only from a model that hears the vocal. |
| Wan 3.0 Prime singing to the song hard-cut at 9.9 s instead of craning up, masked or not | Wan's own editing | Seedance 2.5 with the vocal stem made the same crane as one move ([tool 46](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#46-lip-sync-from-the-songs-own-vocal)). |
| A shader guide at 320 × 180 came back soft and blocky: "the MTWTFSS and the next 'pyramid' shared still is all pixellated" | the guide's detail was too low | A supersampled 1080p render as the guide, with one still per object ([tool 50](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#50-shader-worlds-as-seedance-guides)). |
| At full resolution the paper shot drifted half a second and swapped objects: the Enigma rotor became a helix, the weekday cells lost their letters | a sharp guide with no still per object | One still per object, made from the crisp frames, each named in the prompt with its time. |
| Big-motion singing takes re-sang the vocal instead of copying it | events in the prompt that make a sound: clunks, cannons, gulping, a voice box glitching | Write every action as silent: "Every action in this video is silent: the only sound is @Audio1." ([tool 62](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#62-a-singer-among-screens-of-her-memories)) |
| A "voice-box glitch" written in words drew a broken face: rolled-up eyes, a stretched black mouth | the model drew the glitch on her | Picture-only glitches, her face always intact; the song's glitches go on her head afterwards ([tool 53](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#53-the-head-glitch-on-the-songs-hits)). |
| Her head came back on the motion guide's white shell instead of her grown boom | a video of the character's own body carries the body over | Turn the guide into a coarse blockout (greyscale, flattened, heavily blurred), name it as one, and give her body in words. |
| "0:54 - lip sync bad, need to reshoot." | the vocal window began inside a word, the held "s" of the line before; another line's window began on "(pass)ed" and was re-sung in three takes | Start every window on a clean onset, in a word gap ([tool 14](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#14-the-clean-vocal-window)). |
| Memory images took over the room late in a take, or became shots of their own | the model turned a reference into the scene | Each memory "only as picture content inside the screens' glass, never as the room"; keep the seconds the shots use, or put the screens' content in words. |
| "1:01 scene - she's not lip synced really, are we feeding in vocal stems?" | a take of her farther back, loose on the line before the stutter | Nail the line before the glitch, every word's onset from the lead stem written into the prompt, and let the mouth glitch cover the held stutter. Make a few takes and let the director pick by eye: "can you show me so i can look visually at the lip syn cand choose", then "3". |
| A take began mouthing at "cake", a second late | the take came back that way | Check the first words of every take by eye before picking it. |
| The chatbot's answer sat off the bottom of the kiosk's screen: "the france chat message is just off the bottom of the computer screen" | the take placed it there | A retake with both bubbles inside the screen; the HUD carries only her intercept of the question. |
| Chell jumping into a portal "looked v off bc we used a video model" | a video model's physics | Record the physics in the game itself: six shots of the final were recorded in Portal 2. |
| "glados in your renders and chell etc basically had no movement. it was just her static." | no motion reference, and little motion in words | The boom's motion from a recording of GLaDOS's moves as a rough guide, or written into every second of the timeline. |
| On draft 8, at 1:06: "She needs to be farther away and […] glitching still." | a take that lunged at the lens with her mouth open on every hit | Reshoot her farther back, and build the glitch on her head hit by hit ([tool 54](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#54-glitches-that-build-and-her-mouth)). |
| "to continue" came 0.36 s early after "permission" | Seedance shortens the pauses inside a line | Measure each phrase and place it on its own; ease between offsets in the breath gaps ([tool 69](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#69-lip-sync-phrase-by-phrase)). |
| A take out of sync on its first words; another dropped whole words | one window left only 0.26 s before the first word; another opened inside the held note of the line before | Open every window in silence, half a second to a second before the first word. |
| A take lost the copy of its vocal | 1.6 s of silence before her first word | A lead-in of half a second to a second, no longer. |
| A garbled glass dialog in front of her: "Windows nects our permision" | the prompt had her "lit by a glowing permission dialog" | Never ask a video model for interface or text: the coded interface draws it beside her. |
| A dance take jumped back to its first pose at 7.6 s and held it | the model, unasked | Scan every take for hidden cuts and held frames ([tool 70](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#70-hidden-cuts-and-held-frames-in-a-take)). |
| A take turned her back through a sung line, and came in closer than its first frame | a turn asked for across the words | Turns go between lines; check the framing against the first frame. |
| "her head is alittle cutoff by your green border", then "this shouldnt be so hard something is off" | the first frame, a still set at 80 % on its own green, had faded her crown into the green, and every take made from it carried that | Fix the first frame, not the key: one flat green from edge to edge, her whole crown inside it ([tool 71](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#71-takes-on-green-the-first-frame-the-key-and-the-dances-phase)). |
| Her face drifted off her sheet when she turned to wave | the take was made from a back view, with no picture of her face | Her sheet as a reference whenever her face may show, even small, even from behind ([Seedance](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/seedance/#a-face-needs-her-sheet)). |
| A climax close-up looked soft | a 720p take shown at 1.5× | 1080p wherever her face is shown large. |
| A first-person take looked down into the drop on a fingertip, which filled with the magnified fingertip instead of the world | the camera rose over the drop | Keep the lens level with the drop, in words. |
| A one-second cross-dissolve between two framings in a build take; a ghosted double exposure in a crane | a first and a last frame generated separately, with two cameras | Make the last frame as an edit of the first, and write the camera locked or as one continuous move ([tool 77](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#77-last-frames-made-on-the-first-and-takes-that-continue)). |
| The next take jumped at the seam | it started on the frame the take before was asked to reach, an edit 1.7 % larger than the book | A take that continues another starts on that take's own last frame. |
| Takes came back 0.6 s early to 0.4 s late, each phrase by its own amount, and some sang a line 10–16 % slower | Seedance moves the silences and sings at its own pace | Align each take as a path ([tool 81](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#81-sync-as-a-path-each-take-aligned-to-its-window)). |
| 0.5 to 0.9 s of silence at a full stop where the song dips 0.3 s (three takes of one line), and 0.33 s where it dips 0.1 s (another line, in its take in the film) | a full stop in the prompt's words | Write a line sung through with a comma; check the take's own sound for a gap its window doesn't have, and run the map through it by hand. |
| A take without a soundtrack shut her lips on "better" 0.3 to 0.45 s late, though a fit of mouth against level read it in sync | the line laid on her mouth's whole stretch of singing; a sung line's level is flat | Anchor every b, m and p on the frame where her lips part ([tool 82](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#82-takes-without-a-soundtrack-placed-by-her-lips)). |
| "Mirror, mirror, [0.7 s] on the wall" sung straight through, twice | a take without a soundtrack keeps no pause inside a line, even when the prompt describes it | Make a line with a real pause two segments, or bend the take under a steadied camera ([tool 84](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#84-a-re-timed-take-under-a-steady-camera)). |
| A push-in juddered and surged where the map bent a take for her lips | a slow map repeats frames, and the camera's speed follows the map | Mix neighbouring frames, and re-frame each frame to where a straight playback's camera would be. |
| A pop as a take starts to move | its first frame is the input still, sharper than the rest | Never show a take's first two frames; move cuts off holds. |
| Rolled eyes showing the whites | "her eyes lifting to just above the lens" | Never ask for a look just above the lens; in that take, her eyes on the lens or on something in front of her. In every take, "eyes on the lens" reads as a stare (below) ([Seedance](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/seedance/#directing-her-on-a-locked-camera)). |
| Her head turned right round; her face went off-model looking down | "nods toward the tower behind her"; "looking from it to us" | Point behind her with a hand while she faces the camera. |
| Her head left the top of the frame, and white tights and red shoes appeared | "steps backward to the bed and sits", and a look that named no legwear | On a locked framing, let her move on her mark (turns, gestures, a step toward us) rather than away from the camera, and name every garment that can come into view. |
| After FABLE's release, viewers read her as stiff and frozen, and as unhappy, even menacing | every take carried posture rules ("Her head stays upright on a straight neck: no head tilt", "she faces the camera with her whole body"), and take after take added her eyes on the lens and mood words ("dry", "knowing", "mock innocence"); the video model did each one literally, and together they froze her | Upright and face-on is for her reference sheet. A take gets her movement in words, one loose clause per segment, or a motion reference; emotional words chosen on purpose, warm by default; precise only where it matters, loose elsewhere; a fix stays with the take it fixed ([The recipe](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/recipe/#writing-a-prompt-for-a-model-that-does-exactly-what-it-reads)). |
| Five white flickers in the puppets' eyes; ears removed so they could spring up; a rope grown out of the moon | a puppet's own features, or a prop, scripted to change | Script only what a hand-worked puppet can do: "their painted eyes stay as they are". |
| The last stage of the build read as a morph, the disc swelling and flashing, the hall snapping into shelves | the change was written as one shape becoming another | Write the mechanics fold by fold: "like a row of dominoes … a curved paper bookshelf stands up on a crease in its place". |

## Filters and providers

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Close-up references declined | the provider's face filter | Free, and final for that image on that service. Send the same unaltered image elsewhere, or keep the 2.5D plate. |
| A retry ladder (stronger grade → posterised grade) got takes through, baked banding into them, and was blocked by the harness | altering a reference to pass a safety filter | Never alter an image to pass a filter. A blocked action is a stop, not a puzzle. |
| Jobs fail with no reason, credits back seconds later | a silent input filter misreading innocent wording ("a plug pushed deep into each ear" for foam earplugs) | Reword plainly and keep the beat: plain rewording fixed five of six at once. |
| "output audio may be related to copyright restrictions" | the provider's audio filter | Retry once with a re-cut window, then try the other provider. |
| A filter that passed faces two days ago now declines them | providers change | Keep a second provider configured. |
| The agent's context floods during uploads | presigned-upload replies of about 3.5k characters per file | Upload by URL. |
| A sung opening blocked four times in three stagings, the last from a clearly adult remake | unclear: every blocked attempt carried the same vocal, while other takes of her cuffed beside guards passed | Stop and ask the director. Re-stage it as a genuinely different shot, or drop it. Never route around a block: no silent take with the vocal lip-synced on afterwards. |
| A plane beside a star was blocked | probably read as a plane flying into the sun | Compose it calmly, with the star well clear of the plane. |
