| Seedance's output filter blocked a dance in white satin twice, from two different first frames | unclear; the same dance passed on Wan, and a later drop dance in a red coat passed on Seedance | Make it on the other model. Both blocks were refunded. |
| A leaning pose, pointing at the lens, refused by the provider's content filter | probably the leaning staging | Restage it upright, pointing up at the post above her. |
| Three sung shots refused by the provider's content filter, then a reworded retake and a restaged one too | not stated by the provider | Refused, no take; stop and ask the director, re-stage as a genuinely different shot or drop it. |
| A previz close-up of the performer bringing a pill to her lips refused by the provider's content filter as an input, reworded or not | the guide clip | Refused, no take; re-stage it as a different shot or drop it. |
| WHITEPILL: her face sheet refused by the provider's content filter on Replicate, even alone with a harmless prompt | not stated by the provider | WHITEPILL ran only shots with no face image there. |
| A grey motion-capture body given as a dance reference was refused by the provider's content filter | a nude grey body | No undressed figures as references; describe the dance in words. |

## Spend

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Every submit returns 403 while the account has credit | the API key has its own spend limit | Set the key's limit above the project cap. |
| "Remaining budget" figures are wrong | the local ledger isn't the bill, and it counted free declines | Quote spend only from the provider. |
| Hundreds of credits spent in minutes on unread prompts | a credit-reset deadline drove the spending | Never let a deadline drive spend. |
| A background workflow could still spend after a quality flag | not every spender was stopped | Stop every workflow that can spend: search each for its generate calls. |
| Credits vanished at renewal | subscription credits don't roll over, and top-ups expire | Plan spend inside the period. |
| $148.10 of the $357.51 spent after refunds went to takes the final doesn't show; on four re-light samples: "kinda a waste on the excess ones" | shots re-lit before their outfits and compositions changed, and eight swaps into a look that was then dropped | Fixes, then reshoots, then re-lights. Re-light a shot only once its composition is final. |
| The runner's ledger read $10.40 low | it priced Wan's passes by their generated seconds and left out the input video | Price a video input per second too. |
| "in the future let me give you explicit approval before you do extra gens." | a follow-up generation went out without asking | Ask before any generation the director hasn't approved, cheap or not. |
| A whole-film Wan reshoot, $132.42 at list, dropped as a whole | the method was judged on the whole film, not first on one shot | Try a new method on one shot, several ways, side by side, before the film. |
| Takes sent out in pairs, for a choice | a second take made for every job, used or not | One take per job, judged before the next; a re-roll only when it fails, from better inputs. |

## Colour and look

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| v1 "way too gray … loses the Midjourney magic" | a mono print pass, and chapters desaturating the footage | Colour halftone or native colour; never desaturate the footage. |
| "color grading looked insane"; blue graphics "clash" | a graded look, and a blue accent over blue footage | Native colour; pick the accent against the footage's hue; draw with semantic colour tokens. |
| Flicker in a graded clip | per-frame grading | One LUT per clip, computed from 16 sampled frames. |
| The master looks washed out ("v blown out") | an untagged or BT.601 stream | Convert to BT.709 and tag it; verify with ffprobe. |
| Re-lit shots came back darker and cooler (warm grey paper from a mean level of about 172 to about 111) or brighter (a dark scene from about 34 to about 53) | Wan shifts colour, and never by the same amount twice | One global per-channel match per shot before the splice ([tool 39](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#39-the-colour-match)). |
| The cloud field came back sunset gold: "wayy too saturated compoared to teh pastel light colors of the rest" | the guide was a sunset render and its still was made in the film's saturated look | A day variant of the shader and a pastel still made without the look reference ([tool 50](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#50-shader-worlds-as-seedance-guides)). |
| Shader scenes remastered from the render alone still looked like computer renders | nothing showed the model the materials | Stills of the key moments repainted in the film's look, given with the render. |
| "I feel like we don't get a super aperture vibe" | the shots recorded in Portal 2 dim and foggy (whites at Y′ 50–62, blacks at 9%); the generated chambers' walls grey and their casts scattered | Measure every shot, normalise it, and lay one look over all of it as a tone curve and targeted chroma moves, baked per shot ([tool 57](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#57-the-per-shot-grade)). |
| A cyan-white portal core turned pink | white balance tinted a clipped channel, which holds no colour | Send near-whites that were already clipped to neutral before the look. |
| A +1 stop gain clipped before the shoulder could roll it off | 8-bit level filters | Bake the gain and the look into one float LUT per shot, applied in 16-bit. |
| Each continuation of the far shot of her lost about three points of the palette's score | each link of a chain of takes, made from the last frame of the one before, darkened the picture | One take from the still itself; score every take against the palette ([tool 67](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#67-the-palette-measured-from-the-references)). |
| A falling drop of water turned pink, off the palette | the take | The cut leaves before it. |

## Motion design and the renderer

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| A crop cut her head off after a re-take | code tuned to the old take | Re-frame every shot whose take changed. |
| The previous frame's overlay "sticks" in dense frames | a GPU-backed 2D canvas under software GL | Software-backed canvases, and the history check in QA. It took about two hours of bisecting to find. |
| Frames differ depending on what rendered before | a WebGL canvas drawn into a 2D canvas switches it to GPU rasterisation | Read 2.5D pixels back through the CPU. |
| 0.5–1.1 s a frame on 2.5D shots | the 64-step parallax shader | Depth slices or multiplanes. |
| Tags never finish typing on short shots | the default typing speed | Type at 16–40 characters a second, and finish 6 frames before the cut. |
| A lyric word half hidden on its first frame ("You dor't") | occlusion on the entering row | Tuck an edge only, and switch occlusion off for the entering row. |
| Five accent-coloured elements in one frame | the accent used for every highlight | The accent goes on at most two elements. |
| A snap reads early | keyed 70 ms before its kick | Key moves on hit times from the hits file. |
| Two on-screen numbers disagree ("x380" against "135 RUNNING") | two devices driven separately | Drive both from one value. |
| Shake in a drumless intro | a move that answers no sound | Moves answer audible sounds. Stillness where the song breathes. |
| The same helpers written 8–10 times, slightly differently | chapters couldn't share code | One shared device library. Chapters write only what is unique. |
| The default renderer drew only lyrics | the board's graphics were stored as prose | Structured fields in the board: type, devices, treatment, transition. |
| A lyric time patched in chapter code | fixing the time instead of the alignment | Fix the timed words and re-export. |
| A chapter replaced the default renderer and lost lyrics | the chapter must draw every token itself | Run the lyric gate per chapter, and mark custom-drawn tokens. |
| Fonts that can't be shipped | AGPL, GPL, EULA or unlicensed fonts | Ship OFL fonts only, with their licence texts. |
| A depth model that forbids commercial use | Depth Anything V2 Large is CC-BY-NC | Use Depth Anything V2 Small, which is Apache-2.0. |
| A singing mouth held where the take isn't synced | the edit fell back to a plate | Crops, inserts or depth moves on those words. |
| A famous card "too different/ broken up so we lose the reference" | a pastiche: small, tilted, split across two cards, shaking, colour-fringed | Rebuild the real one from measured frames, whole and full frame. |
| A touch landed on the interface's side rail after the interface was rebuilt | a coordinate typed from the old layout | Pin touches, lyrics and tags to the interface's layout table, and take hand-off boxes from the code that draws them. Never retype numbers. |
| The level tag covered the interface's title | one corner for the whole film | Place the tag per scene, move it only on a cut, and match it across chapter seams. |
| A real wordmark on a costume came back blank or garbled | generators can't spell a logo | Composite the real mark in code, tracked to the costume and lit by the frame. |
| A dive through visor after visor flickered: four flashes in one second | single-frame bright pops as lit rims rushed past the lens | Ramp each pass over three frames or more; flag any frame brighter or darker than both neighbours by more than 0.03. Check per chapter: this one was found after the encode. |
| "at like 4 seconds the ramp trace decouples from the ramp" | a line drawn once over footage whose camera zooms | Read the real edge from the frame as drawn, every frame. |
| "the end of the scrolling up ramp clip starts to show curve down, so it should be cut earlier" | the window ran past what the shot should show | A window ends where the picture stops being right for the shot, not only where the model breaks. |
| "the temporary half-shown cut of claudia" | a move from a real frame to her with no last frame to aim for, landing in a dim dissolve | A first-and-last-frame move that ends on her. |
| Impact effects buried the car | smears decaying over 0.12–0.28 s | The impact frame stays sharp; the smear peaks on the second frame and is gone by the fourth. |
| "the app notification shade is too small for the text … has no proper margins"; "rounded corners not mathematically precise" | an interface drawn by eye | Measure the real one: iOS 26's insets and gaps, continuous corners, platters that grow to fit their text. |
| "the upper line overlaps infront of the top line on the E" | a letter built from separate bars | Draw it as one extruded outline. |
| "the time limit is behind some scenes and infront of others" | layering by draw order | Layer each element by its own plane in depth. |
| "the entire top and bottom parts of the frame go black, interpreted as massive jitter" | the walls of reels paged a full screen on every vocal chop and smeared into black bands | The room answers the beat lightly: the kicks and her landings nudge it by 15 % of what they did. |
| Black vertical lines that "appear occasionally": dark columns on every 8th frame of one shot | one of eight render workers drew its share from a stale camera state | Scan every final for single-frame outliers ([tool 43](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#43-the-single-frame-outlier-scan)). |
| A tunnel strobed and the flash check passed it: 29 of 144 cells alternated light and dark for nine frames | the near cards swapped bright and dark every frame | Scan every full render for strobes cell by cell; fade near cards and smear every card. |
| A one-frame blink at a chapter's edge | the boundary frame was rendered by the neighbour's old code | Re-render a changed chapter with a frame of padding on each side, and check every cut on a seam sheet. |
| Later chapters drew their edges differently | one 2D canvas made without the software flag moved the frame onto the GPU, and a worker carries it across chapters | Make every 2D canvas software-backed. |
| Lyrics built into the scene as objects sat "haphazardly in space": "like im the white pill is a weird curve" | an image model placed the words in 3D by eye | Draw the lyrics after, small and classical, one line at a time ([Motion](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/motion/#a-lyric-video)). |
| A 2D animation given to Wan as its video: "it followed the pills animation too closely - like, it moved the pills around perfectly with the animation, so despite relighting them they still looked a little amateuirsh" | a video model keeps a video's layout and motion | Give a video model as video only what must move exactly; the rest as stills or in words. |
| A shader shot lost its last frames | its song was muxed in with `-shortest` | Count every render's frames against its shot. |
| Full-frame glitches: "i dont rly like the full frame glitches much at all" | the glitch pass tore the whole picture on every hit | No full-frame glitch: her head glitches inside a matte, on the song's own hits, short unless asked for longer ([tool 53](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#53-the-head-glitch-on-the-songs-hits)). |
| Text placed on the monitors "just faceplant - its not on th emonitor at all" | text tracked onto a moving screen by a naive pass | Drop the tracking: elements in their own space, and world tags only where a track holds on every frame. |
| "all the drawn on panels need to be tilted hte other way in 3d - the small side is on the outside and long end is inside -r everse so it feels like a hud." | each panel turned on its own hinge | One visor round the eye: anything near a side has its long edge outside by construction ([tool 55](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#55-a-hud-from-one-visor-and-one-projector)). |
| "the pop-up panels are on a different surface than the memory one" | panels and projections drawn as separate cards, each with its own turn and its own look | One visor and one projector: one bloom, one raster, one chromatic offset, and no cards. |
| The arrest film's net "is the same color with no outlines around it in blue, so there's no contrast with the platform that it's put on" | the subject in its floor's grey, with no outline | The subject in a strong colour with a dark outline, its values apart from the floor, checked at the HUD's size ([tool 61](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#61-insert-films-that-read-at-hud-size)). |
| A white-only hologram pass flattened the orange net again | the projection turned every colour into the visor's white | The projection keeps the film's colour key: strong colour stays itself. |
| An insert's RAM bites were dark specks at 380 px | small subjects, drawn for the film's full size | Big, bright subjects in full view, checked at 380–480 px. |
| "the line across the center of teh screen at 0:01 second - remove that entirely" | a boot scan line drawn across her sight | Boot rows only, and nothing across her sight. |
| "the 0:08-0:13 animation has the memory words too subtle" | a small title block in a corner | The title the full width of the left column, behind her stand. |
| The memory film's first frames: "stuff is overlapping, assets are not well layered" | an SVG layout with no check | A real isometric render, and a layout check on every frame: a frame that fails isn't written ([tool 60](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#60-a-memory-film-with-her-own-face)). |
| The head glitch's matte took a column of monitors, or the wall of screens under her | SAM2 on a small or far head | Look at the mattes' QC sheet every time, and cut the matte to a head zone from the face box ([tool 54](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#54-glitches-that-build-and-her-mouth)). |
| "The sun is off the widget for example - just broken" | the gadgets not at the system's real sizes, and the Weather's art not clipped to its panel | Rebuild an interface at its real sizes: five gadgets fit, and each plays a part ([tool 65](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#65-a-desktop-recreated-in-code)). |
| A window's title ballooned as it maximised | the window stretched as a picture | Draw the window's own layout at every step between its two rectangles. |
| The chapters read an empty song map | the film page's own top-level `let SONG` shadowed the global of the same name for every bare reference | One object under both names. |
| A small picture differed with the render order | Chromium decoded a JPEG drawn small at a reduced scale only when no full decode was cached | Every picture through a 1:1 software copy; check purity in three orders ([tool 20](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#20-the-history-check)). |
| A bitmap depended on which frame drew it first | a cache keyed by a scale under an eased camera | Key caches by their content. |
| "theres a black flash on the screen right after 45 for 0 reason" | the system's real two-frame blink as it switches to the permission prompt | Leave out a real behaviour that reads as a glitch: the dim comes straight off the desktop's own picture. |
| "the wii cursor is totally off lol" | a 3D glove pointer in the 3D world | The engine's flat drawing of a white cartoon glove, swaying with her aim and dipping when pressed. |
| Her step-out take hidden 1.5 cm behind the picture; a glass fish's path across her face; a glass cursor across it on 24 frames | objects placed in 3D without her face in view | Project every object against her face, frame by frame, before the final render ([tool 68](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#68-one-curved-screen-in-3d-the-desktop-as-its-texture)). |
| A ghost band of the boardwalk over the curved screen's desktop | the concave glass slab focused what was behind the camera | Camera rays over the picture pass straight through the glass, with its tint and a sheen of the sky on top. |

## Review

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Runs "completed" with no review at all | a usage limit made reviewers return nothing, and the script read that as "no fixes" | A null review is an explicit failure, in code. Carry open fixes forward. |
| Reviewers scored 6–7.5 a cut the director called "perfect" | a stricter bar than the director's | Ship on "no blocking fix left". Calibrate on the director's verdicts. At most two rounds. |
| A reviewer re-ran checks until its time ran out and wrote nothing | it wasn't told what was authoritative | Bound reviewers by output: "write the short version first". |
| The scan flagged an intended prop | a generic "modern object" rule | Whitelist intended anachronisms by name. |
| A strobe counted twice | the flash check paired every transition | Count opposing pairs. |
| Twelve blocks found in 96 "final" takes | generated people; filters let outputs through | A safety and canon scan of every take before release. |
| First-draft chapters scored 5–6.5: faces printing blank, type over faces, repeated devices | animators with nobody reviewing real renders | A reviewer renders, looks, and writes concrete fixes. |
| Chapters reported done still missed notes: two of four failed their check in one round | animators checking their own work | An independent checker renders every note's moment and reports each note done or not, with evidence; then one refix. |
| The takes' verdicts missed a man in a car's window and a repair that turned into a hatchback | one look per take | An adversarial scout re-checks every take frame by frame before more is spent. |
| A fixer swapped an off-model close-up on another set into a held shot | a chapter fix after the chapter's own reviews | A whole-film critic after the chapter rounds, re-rendering the director's notes and every seam. |
| The lead took the black lines for the gaps between reel columns: "no ur wrong … they appear occasionally, look at more framers" | one frame looked at | Look at many frames around a note, then scan for it. |
| "can you show me exactly what i need to pick? sorry its far back in convo history" | the picks were spread across a long conversation | Put every pick the director owes in one message, numbered, with the images. |
| A re-light judged darker and softer on its own read better in the film: "New better." | it was judged alone, not where it plays | Judge a re-light in context, side by side with the original. |
| The spectrogram comparison called a take re-sung that was in sync by eye | the vocal-stem method re-voices the soundtrack, in the vocal's place | Judge that method by eye with the song laid over ([tool 15](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#15-the-sync-check-the-spectrogram-comparison)). |
| "show me the references you gave the model too" | the references weren't shown with the take | One board of every take's references, sent before anything runs. |
| The sync check called a take diverged on a held, glitched vowel | it stops trusting a take there | Judge it by eye with the song laid over ([tool 63](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#63-placing-a-re-sung-take-by-its-lag)). |
| "show me the green screen roto before you render plz" | cut-outs went into renders unseen | Each key goes out first as a review clip, the green source beside the cut-out, with the song laid over. |
| The book closed, then the mirror spoke from inside it; the shelf and the credit were read at once | the ending cut for timing, not for the story's order | Cut the ending in story order, and let the picture run past the song for the credit. |
| Captions outlived their shots | a print timed to its line, not its shot | A line's print never outlives the shot it is sung in, and leaves before the next one arrives ([tool 87](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#87-the-annotated-edition-and-the-916-page)). |
| The author stopped seeing what a viewer sees | it had made every frame | Two fresh-eyes reviewers on one sheet per shot before each delivery; fix what is a fault, list what is a choice ([tool 88](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#88-two-fresh-eyes-reviews)). |

## Render and running agents

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Nobody knew the encode had finished | it ran as a detached job | Tracked background jobs with a status. |
| Swap and the root disk filled up | six agents rendering at once, with frames on the small system disk | One rendering workflow at a time, scratch on the big disk, and check free memory and disk first. |
| Disk full after a render | about 9.6 GB of frames per cut | Delete the frames once ffprobe has verified the outputs. |
| Commands ran against the wrong project | an export inside a backgrounded shell chain | Name the project on every command. |
| A merge restarted three times (about 1.5 h) | an interrupt kills every running workflow | Short phases, run ids saved, resume by run id. |
| One serial chapter workflow would have taken about 12 h | serial agents | Three parallel workflows (about 4 h). |
| A ~20-hour background queue, new takes stuck behind superseded ones | post-processing auto-queued on every import | Queue only takes the edit uses, in priority order. Cancel superseded jobs. |
| A shared machine at 100% CPU, every job 3–5× slower | two dozen waiters polling every 3 s | One shared listing every 45 s for all waiters. |
| Duplicate jobs after a restart | killing a waiter left its child behind, and the re-run resubmitted | Record job ids beside their inputs, adopt queued jobs, and kill orphans by id. |
| Every new agent session fails at start | an agent CLI auto-updated mid-run | Pin versions for long jobs. Check the job's error before assuming there is no work. |
| A worker probed for 75 minutes and delivered nothing | no bound on the first deliverable | A first complete draft within about 10 commands, with a mandatory handoff. |
| Shared-file bugs fixed differently in parallel chapters | workers patching shared code | Workers report shared bugs; the operator fixes them once. |
| A resumed multi-chapter workflow reviewed and fixed chapters that had already finished | the resume replayed its stages unevenly | One workflow per chapter, with the notes in files the agents re-read. |
| Three chapter runs interrupted three times mid-build | an interrupt ends every running agent | Resume each from where it stopped: only the agents that were cut off run again (57 of 147 launches), and finished work is kept. |
| Rotos killed for lack of memory; one came back with 35 of 210 mattes and looked like success | the matting library's CPU memory arena held about 12.5 GB per 1080p take on a box shared with renders, and a `\| tail` hid the exit status | Arena off (1.3 GB); count the mattes against the frames and fail loudly ([tool 41](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#41-roto-on-a-cpu-box)). |
| Six chapter launches interrupted mid-build | an interrupt ends a running agent | Each animator keeps a notes file; the relaunch reads it and picks up where the last stopped. |
| One seed with the same inputs gave three different previz takes | the previz model isn't reproducible run to run | Keep the take file; a seed doesn't pin a take. |
| A previz take with a jump inside it passed the automatic cut check | the check looked for cuts | Check every pick for jumps as well, with the cut measure of the assembly ([tool 44](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#44-the-bar-map-as-the-timeline)). |
| The cut ran about 0.9 s behind the song by its end | parts from stills or padded with `tpad` started a frame late, and the concat summed the gaps | Stamp every part's frame n at n/24 ([tool 64](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#64-frame-exact-parts-and-decoding)). |
| From 1:48.5 on, every tool that counted decoded frames was one frame late | a default decode duplicated a frame once the concat's 0.7 ms a part had added up | Decode with `-vsync passthrough` wherever frames are counted, and seek a still by its own timestamp. |
| The last 2 s of a stream went missing | the song muxed in the same pass as the encode | Encode the picture alone, then copy the song onto it. |
| A 1,325-frame video from a 1,949-frame sequence | `.png` names linked to JPEG data, and ffmpeg's image2 demuxer dropped every one of them | Convert to the named format, and count the decoded frames against the sequence ([tool 25](https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/toolkit/#25-encode-and-deliver)). |
| A tool read the frames before the song wrongly | a picture that starts before the song has negative frame numbers | Parse a leading minus in every frame range, and pass it as `--frames=-64-1884`, so no command line takes it for an option. |
| numpy broke for every tool in one folder | a script there was named after a standard-library module (`numbers.py`) | Never name a script after a standard-library module. |

## Publishing

| What you see | Why | The rule now |
|---|---|---|
| Identifying details in a making-of: names, profile codes, hosts, job ids | raw production notes | Scrub rules, a grep pass, and two fresh-eyes reads. |
| A song file carries the generator's song id in its tags | file metadata | Strip metadata from everything you publish. Midjourney images carry their job id in XMP. |
| Real-person likeness risk | generated portraits of real people | Keep generated likenesses of real people out; quote their words as text, with the source. CLODYSSEY's labelled AI IMAGE post cards are left out of this site. |
| A master posted without the AI disclosure | platform toggles missed | Set each platform's AI-content label, and name the tools. |

From the Claudia wiki: https://claudiagallery.vip/wiki/failures/


---

# Use her

Claudia is an open character. What you can do with her and the images here, and what isn't covered.


Claudia is an open character. Make images, videos, songs, stories, games or merch with her, commercial or not. Use the
images on this site as references, as image prompts, or as material. You don't need to ask. A credit ("Claudia by
anabology") is appreciated, not required.

## What helps

- **Keep her herself.** The [canon](https://claudiagallery.vip/claudia/) is short: the black bob, one clay streak, the star clip, the mic, an
  adult face. Change everything else.
- **Make her an adult, always.** She is in her late twenties. Nothing that reads under-age, and nothing explicit.
- **Say what's generated.** The first nine films were made with Midjourney, Seedance, Suno and Claude (AIRPLANE MODE also
  with GPT-6 Astra agents in Blender, DOWNFORCE also with Wan 3.0 over real footage, DON'T LET ME SCROLL also with Wan
  3.0, WHITEPILL also with MiniMax H3 for its previz, Wan 3.0 Prime and GPT Image 2.5, THE CAKE IS NOT A LIE also with
  GPT Image 2.5, Blender renders and six shots recorded in Portal 2, AERO also with GPT Image 2.5, Blender renders and
  TripoSG's meshes), and FABLE with Claude, GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst, Seedance and Suno, its sets painted in code and no
  Midjourney at all; each said so.

## Songs with her

She is open to musicians the way Hatsune Miku is open to producers: make songs with her and release them. A few norms
keep it clean for everyone.

- **Release under your own name.** You are the artist. Never upload as "anabology": that is the director's artist
  profile, and anything released there reads as theirs. Don't present a release as an official Claudia or anabology
  release.
- **Leave "feat. Claudia" out of the artist field.** Streaming services match artist names to profiles, so a "Claudia"
  credit merges into unrelated artists already called Claudia, or creates a profile that whoever claims it controls.
- **Credit her in the description and on the cover:** "Claudia is an open character by anabology (claudiagallery.vip)".
- **If any of it is AI-made, say so.** Vocals, music or lyrics: distributors ask, and the services label it. Human-made
  work needs no label. For AI tools, check the terms for commercial release (Suno, for one, requires a paid plan at the
  time you make the song).
- **Make your own songs.** Don't re-release the songs of ESCAPE VELOCITY, CLODYSSEY, BLISS, AIRPLANE MODE, DOWNFORCE,
  DON'T LET ME SCROLL, WHITEPILL, THE CAKE IS NOT A LIE, AERO or FABLE, or their stems.
- **One place for fan tracks:** a fan-run playlist works better than a shared artist profile, because nobody has to own it.

## What isn't covered

- **Other people's things in the films.** The Bliss photograph and the XP sounds belong to Microsoft. Real public figures
  appear in CLODYSSEY as posts labelled AI IMAGE, and AIRPLANE MODE shows real posts (Elon Musk's on a lock screen in the
  boarding, others in one episode); none of them is part of this gallery's images. The anime idol in CLODYSSEY is
  another creator's character. AIRPLANE MODE rebuilds real things in code (the 2004 anti-piracy card, an airline's
  seat-back screen, Anthropic's marks on the guards' patches); they belong to their owners. DOWNFORCE is cut from
  Tesla's livestream of the Roadster demo (15 October 2026) and SpaceX's 2018 Starman footage, and its numbers are read
  off Tesla's on-screen telemetry; the footage, the telemetry and the cars belong to their owners, and none of it is
  among this gallery's images. Its lyric quotes words said on stage that night and the last line of *Back to the
  Future*. DON'T LET ME SCROLL draws real interfaces in code after the real ones: X, Instagram's reels, Pinterest,
  LinkedIn, Google Chrome, Facebook's tracking prompt and Apple's iOS 26 (the Dynamic Island, Screen Time, the lock
  screen, Liquid Glass), with the TSLA and SPACEX tickers and Alexander Graham Bell's 1876 telephone patent drawing (US
  174,465). The apps, their designs and their marks belong to their owners. Its posts are fictional, and the stock ticker
  with her name is made up. WHITEPILL's lyric and pictures refer to real things by their names: Skynet and its hour,
  2:14, from *Terminator 2*; the red and blue pills of *The Matrix*; 42 and Deep Thought from *The Hitchhiker's Guide to
  the Galaxy*; Keynes's 1930 forecast of a fifteen-hour week; the Enigma I's rotor wiring; ubiquitin from the Protein
  Data Bank (1UBQ); and SpaceX's drone ship *Of Course I Still Love You*, named after a ship of the Culture novels,
  with a landed booster. Its look was asked for in the manner of Wes Anderson's films, and its previz took its
  dance moves from clips of adult dancers in public dance videos, as motion references only: none of their footage is in
  the film. These belong to their owners. THE CAKE IS NOT A LIE is a fan film set in Valve's Portal 2: Portal and Portal
  2, Aperture Science, GLaDOS, Chell, Cave Johnson, the turrets, the personality cores, the cake and "the cake is a lie"
  are Valve's. Six of its shots were recorded in Portal 2, its interface is set in Portal 2's own type and pictograms, and
  the Aperture logo on its end card is redrawn to match a reference the director sent. Its song and lyric are its own; its
  final chorus ends by turning the title of the 2025 book *If Anyone Builds It, Everyone Dies*, and its verses sing the
  month's AI news. AERO is shot inside Windows Vista recreated in code: Windows Vista and Windows 7, Aero, the User
  Account Control prompt, Windows Live Messenger, Windows Media Player, Photo Gallery, Flip 3D and the Bubbles
  screensaver are Microsoft's, as are Vista's wallpaper (Aurora), shown in the film, and the interface sounds of Vista and
  Windows Live Messenger that its mix plays in the song's key. Its advert parodies Microsoft's 2009 "I'm a PC" campaign.
  The Wii is Nintendo's; the bowling and tennis on its desktop are drawn for the film. Its look follows reference videos
  the director picked: their frames were the style references of its Midjourney worlds and, with pictures from a
  Frutiger Aero moodboard, of its 2008 pictures; its dances took their moves from recordings of a dancer, as motion
  references only. None of that material is in the film.
  The headline in its news gadget is Ember's (Global Electricity Mid-Year Insights, 2025). FABLE retells public-domain
  tales (Snow White's mirror, the Ant and the Grasshopper, Jack and the Beanstalk, the Tortoise and the Hare, Red Riding
  Hood, the Elves and the Shoemaker, Pinocchio, Rapunzel, the house that Jack built); its silhouette film is drawn in
  code in the manner of Lotte Reiniger's cut-card films, and its six made-things are the golem, the sorcerer's broom,
  Frankenstein's creature, Pinocchio, the robots of 1920 and the machine-woman of 1927. Its lyric reads that week's
  public news about AI (an Anthropic stock listing, local ballot measures on data centres, a Nasdaq drop, an Anthropic
  essay, the model's system card), and the spines on its shelf carry the names of Anthropic's models. These belong to
  their owners.
- **Anthropic.** Claudia is fan work about Claude. She is not affiliated with or endorsed by Anthropic, and Anthropic's
  names and marks are theirs.
- **The director's accounts.** The Midjourney profile and the Suno Voice used in the films live in personal accounts and
  can't be shared. Everything they made is here.

## Credits

Directed by **anabology**. Made with **Claude** (Anthropic's model, in Claude Code) as the production team, **Midjourney**
v8.2 for every image of the first nine films, **Seedance 2.5** for the moving shots and **Suno** for the songs (v6 where the records name it).
AIRPLANE MODE's game world and the motion references for its VR shots were built in **Blender** by **GPT-6 Astra**
agents (OpenAI's model), briefed and checked by Claude. DOWNFORCE's 3D moves and most of its shots of her were made with
**Wan 3.0**, its repairs and re-shoots with Seedance 2.5, and it is cut from **Tesla**'s livestream of the Roadster demo
and **SpaceX**'s 2018 Starman footage. DON'T LET ME SCROLL's takes were made with Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5, re-dressed
and re-lit with Seedance's video edits and repaired with Wan, and played inside a world drawn in code. WHITEPILL was
prevized with **MiniMax H3** (its opening with **Wan 3.0 Prime**) and shot in Seedance 2.5, singing from Suno's own stem
of the song's vocal; its worlds are GLSL shaders written by Claude, and a cloud field supplied by anabology, filmed as
real things by Seedance 2.5; its stills and image edits were made with Midjourney and **GPT Image 2.5**, and a
whole-film reshoot in Wan 3.0 Prime was tried and dropped. THE CAKE IS NOT A LIE's song is anabology's own Suno take, its
lead vocal through a treatment anabology chose by ear, with 15 % of the untreated voice under it; its shots were made in
Seedance 2.5 from first frames made with Midjourney and GPT Image 2.5, and six were recorded in Portal 2; its memory film
and insert films are **Blender** renders, its head mattes **SAM2**'s; and its HUD, its glitches and its grade were made in
code by Claude. AERO's song is a Suno take anabology picked from Claude's rounds and gave a new ending; the film was shot
inside a Vista desktop Claude coded and rendered in headless Chromium, its first 1:20 and its drop also rendered in
Blender with glass objects made into meshes by **TripoSG**; her takes are Seedance 2.5 from first frames GPT Image 2.5
made in Midjourney's worlds or on green, lip-synced from Suno's split of the lead vocal; its loops are Midjourney's video model's, and
its interface sounds were re-pitched with **Rubber Band**. FABLE was written, painted and directed by **Claude Fable 5.2**
on its release day, from anabology's brief and plan sign-off: its thirteen set plates were painted in SVG, in code, by
the lead and three painter agents and rebuilt as paper by **GPT Image 2.6 Sunburst**; every moving shot is Seedance 2.5
(her takes on Higgsfield's API, the paper-only takes on Replicate), lip-synced from Suno's own lead-vocal stem; the
group's voices were separated with **demucs**, the words checked with **faster-whisper**, her lips measured with
**MediaPipe**; its silhouette film was drawn and animated in code; and its song is the Suno v6-wild take anabology
picked by ear for the second version. This site was built by Claude from the films' own records.
